The warranty for a stationary fire pump drive engine starts at the time of purchase or when the engine is first used for fire protection applications. The engine is to be used only for fire protection applications, and Figure 2-2 and Figure 2-3 provide visual descriptions of the engine components for this fire pump drive engine. The latest technology and highest quality components were used to produce this engine. Cummins reserve the right to make changes at any time. If any differences are found between an engine and the information in this manual, contact your local Authorized Repair Location. The latest technology and highest quality components were used to produce this engine. Cummins fire pump drive engines as packaged units (engine and accessories) have been approved by Factory Mutual (FM) Approvals and listed by Underwriter's Laboratories (UL), Inc. And Underwriter's Laboratories of Canada (ULC). When replacement parts are needed, we recommend using only genuine Cummins parts. Injury may result and warranty is voided if fuel rate, revolutions per minute (RPM), or altitudes exceed published maximum values for this model and application. The fire pump drive engine nameplate is shown in Figure 2-1. The fire pump controller starts the engine automatically when the Fire Pump Digital Panel (FPDP) is in auto-mode and a remote fire demand signal is received. The fire pump controller automatically shuts down the engine when the fire demand signal is discontinued. The fire pump controller is optionally supplied by Cummins or Cummins Sales and Service. Upon turning the fire pump controller to OFF, the fire pump drive engine may continue to run at a reduced speed to cool the engine down. The engine starts and operates at the recommended fire pump drive engine speed specification and inspects the following: 1. Check that the engine starts and operates at the proper operating speed. 2. Check that the engine has attained a normal run- ning temperature after running the engine for a minimum of thirty minutes. 3. Check that the engine is operating at the proper operating speed. 4. Check for unusual engine noise. 5. Ensure that the oil pressure is greater than 69 kPa (10 psig). 6. Check that the coolant temperature is between 70°C (158°F) and 107°C (225°F). 7. Check that the engine is operating at the proper operating speed.

The minimum crangking speed for the CFP11E is 120 RPM, while the maximum crangking speed is 2100 RPM. The minimum recommended battery capacity - cold soak at 0°F (-18°C) or above is 24V, while the maximum battery capacity is 6 ft. (1.8 m) long. The minimum resistance of starting circuit is 0.0017 Ohms, and the maximum resistance is 345 Ohms. The operating speed in RPM is 1470, while the average operating speed is 1760. The ventilation air required is 740 litres/sec, while the exhaust gas flow is 875 litres/sec. The heat rejection to coolant is 844 litres/sec, and the engine operates at 977°F (525°C) or 954°F (512°C) depending on the operating system. The air filter service indicator has not popped-up, indicating an air filter blockage. The engine starts and operates properly under normal conditions. The engine stops when the overspeed RESET/STOP switch is pressed until the engine stops. The engine should be serviced and inspected before equipment operation. The factory-set crangk termination setpoint is 600 RPM, and the engine should not be changed from this value.
